rationale.conceptual: The GCMC method with EAM potentials is established but requires careful implementation of the specific cavity geometry and acceptance criteria. Several interacting components (slab, potentials, GCMC moves) and proper physical interpretation make it beyond a simple textbook exercise.
rationale.execution: The workflow consists of 2-3 sequential steps (system setup, Cu/Au simulation, Ag/Au simulation). Each step is a loop over chemical potentials, using standard computational chemistry tools, with straightforward CSV output. No complex data fetching or multi-tool orchestration.

difficulty.reasoning: The task requires replicating Grand Canonical Monte Carlo simulations of metal deposition in nanocavities using EAM potentials, a non-trivial computational chemistry method. Setting up the correct slab geometry, handling EAM potentials, and performing GCMC sampling across many chemical potentials demands domain expertise. The engineering pipeline is straightforward, with only a few sequential steps.

compute_estimate.reasoning: Classical off-lattice GCMC simulation of a few thousand atoms with EAM potentials runs on a single CPU; memory footprint is low, and no large external datasets are needed.
